positions.stance: "Believes we must deport all criminal illegals and secure the border."
Wants to cut taxes for every Kentuckian.
Has defended girls' sports and private spaces from what he calls "the radical trans movement."
Highlights leading the fight for veterans, including passing the Veterans Fairness and Transparency Act.
Says he fought "Biden's war on energy" and that Kentucky energy powers America.

S6KY00385.name: Charles Booker
S6KY00385.bio: Former Kentucky state representative from West Louisville.

positions.stance: Will cut taxes for working and middle-class families, lower costs for necessities, protect Social Security and Medicare, and defend workers' freedom to organize.
Will expand affordable SBA and community lending, cut federal paperwork for employers with fewer than 50 workers, and offer small employers a public health option.
Supports suspending the federal gas tax for a year, allowing year-round E15 sales, and replenishing the Strategic Petroleum Reserve.
Would co-sponsor the Ratepayer Protection Act, the Energy Bills Relief Act, and expanded heating, cooling and weatherization grants.
Will fight for federal dollars to repair roads and bridges, finish rural broadband, and upgrade drinking water and wastewater systems.

S8OR00207.name: Jeff Merkley
S8OR00207.bio: Former leader of nonprofits that created affordable housing.

positions.stance: Supports ending gerrymandering, overturning Citizens United, and required early voting, vote-by-mail, and same-day registration.
"We must invest in a shift to 100% clean and renewable energy sources."
Supports rural high-speed broadband, Medicare for All, and smaller elementary school class sizes.

S6OR05218.name: David Brock Smith
S6OR05218.bio: Third-generation Southwest Oregon resident and small businessman.

positions.stance: Says Oregonians feel their local and federal elected leaders are out of touch, and pledges to put Oregon first.
Says "Oregon families are being priced out of their own state, and businesses are moving across state lines."
Supports law enforcement, calling officers "the blue line that serves and protects us all."
Calls for ending the homelessness crisis, criticizing Oregon's spending of millions on its approach.
Prioritizes wildfire prevention policy, noting "catastrophic wildfires are ever-increasing in Oregon and across the western states."

S6OK04247.name: Kevin Hern
S6OK04247.bio: U.S. Representative from Oklahoma; former aerospace engineer and McDonald's franchise owner.

positions.stance: Supports veterans; cosponsored bills honoring Blue Water Navy and WWII Merchant Mariner veterans.
Supports a balanced budget amendment to address the national debt and curb spending.
Supports securing the border; voted to fund a border wall and cosponsored a bill to defund sanctuary campuses.
Advocates small-business capital access and opposes policies that harm free enterprise.
Supports protecting religious liberty, including Christmas symbols and "so help me God" in oaths.

S6OK04163.name: N'Kiyla Jasmine Thomas
S6OK04163.bio: Nurse, Chickasaw citizen, and active-duty military spouse from Ardmore, Oklahoma.

positions.stance: Says education "should prepare children for life, not politics"; will fight to reduce class sizes and reliance on standardized testing.
"No one working full time should struggle to survive"; supports a living-wage minimum wage and strong price-gouging protections.
"Healthcare is a human right, not a privilege"; supports Medicare for All.
"Decisions about pregnancy belong to patients, not politicians"; will fight to restore Roe v. Wade federally.
Supports universal, affordable childcare, including 24/7 options, treated as federal infrastructure.

S6IA00314.name: Ashley Hinson
S6IA00314.bio: U.S. Representative for Northeast Iowa and member of the House Appropriations Committee.

positions.stance: Believes "it is YOUR money, not the government's money" and focuses on lowering taxes for working families.
Says Iowans everywhere should be able to access quality healthcare without driving hours or worrying about cost.
Calls agriculture "the lifeblood of Iowa's economy" and says farmers need an advocate who understands their challenges.
Says public safety starts with enforcing laws, supporting law enforcement, and securing the border.
Fighting "to restore integrity to public service" so government works for the people.

S6IA00298.name: Josh Turek
S6IA00298.bio: Iowa state legislator and former professional wheelchair basketball athlete.

positions.stance: "Each and every American should be able to afford the basics."
"Health care is a human right. All Americans deserve access to basic care."
"Stop the corruption. Politicians should deliver for the people, not enrich themselves."
"Iowa's farmers are the best in the world. It's time we fight for them"; criticizes tariff and trade policies hurting farmers.
"We must protect and defend our fundamental freedoms", including freedom of speech.

S4AR00103.name: Tom Cotton
S4AR00103.bio: U.S. Senator for Arkansas and former Army infantry officer who served in Iraq and Afghanistan.

positions.stance: "America is a nation of laws, and a country without a border is not a country."
Says he is fighting for even lower prices for working Arkansans.
Highlights keeping Arkansas at the center of America's defense.
"Every Arkansas family deserves safe streets and secure communities."
Supports lower taxes: "Arkansans know how to spend their money better than Washington does."

S6AR00199.name: Hallie Shoffner
S6AR00199.bio: Sixth-generation Arkansas farmer and small-business owner.

positions.stance: Prioritizes lowering costs for working families, saying "costs are too high."
Focuses on growing the economy and supporting the workforce as jobs leave Arkansas.
Supports affordable, accessible healthcare: "No one should have to choose between groceries and going to the doctor."
Pledges to protect Social Security and Medicare.
Supports strengthening unions and protecting workers, saying unions "helped build the middle class."

S8MS00261.name: Cindy Hyde-Smith
S8MS00261.bio: U.S. Senator for Mississippi; former Mississippi Commissioner of Agriculture and Commerce and state senator.

positions.stance: An enhanced-carry permit holder who says she "will always stand up for our 2nd Amendment Constitutional rights."
Pledges to work to pass a Balanced Budget Amendment to the U.S. Constitution.
Believes Obamacare should be repealed and replaced with a patient-centered plan without expanding government's role in health care.
Opposes taxpayer funding of abortions and will vote to confirm pro-life judges.
Believes illegal immigration must end; supports building a wall on the southwestern border and increased immigration enforcement funding.
"Believes a family that works hard should be able to afford groceries, gas and the light bill."
"Believes work should pay fairly."
"Believes nobody should have to choose between seeing a doctor and paying the rent"; aims to save healthcare and hospitals.
Believes Mississippi should welcome investment and that Big Tech should pay its own way.
"Believes public office is a trust, not a business."

S0KS00315.name: Roger Marshall
S0KS00315.bio: OB-GYN from Great Bend and U.S. Senator for Kansas.

positions.stance: Supports phosphate fertilizer relief for Kansas growers; lead sponsor of the Lowering Input Costs for American Farmers Act.
Pledges to protect Kansas's Critical Access hospitals, which make up 82 of the state's 124 hospitals.
Cosponsored the Laken Riley Act and the Build the Wall Act.
Supports "Oil, gas, wind, and Kansas-grown ethanol — no apologies for any of them."
"Kansas builds the planes. We make sure Kansas keeps building them."

S6KS00312.name: Adam Hamilton
S6KS00312.bio: Founding pastor of a Kansas City-area church he has served for 36 years.

positions.stance: Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy, ending tariffs, and requiring data centers to pay their fair share of electricity costs.
Supports expanding Medicare to cover vision and dental and prioritizing reimbursement for home-based care.
Supports banning Wall Street investors from buying single-family homes and tax credits for first-time buyers, firefighters, police officers, and teachers.
Supports expanding Medicare drug price negotiation, reversing Medicaid cuts, and restoring ACA subsidies.
Supports protecting farmers from tariffs, expanding export markets, and passing the full farm bill.

S0NM00058.name: Ben Ray Luján
S0NM00058.bio: U.S. Senator for New Mexico and former U.S. Representative.

positions.stance: Fighting to bring costs down for New Mexico families, including reversing SNAP cuts and making housing more affordable.
Fighting for federal investment in infrastructure, clean energy, manufacturing, workforce training, and National Labs.
Supports community safety investments and has introduced legislation mandating training and accountability for ICE and CBP officers.
"I'll work with anyone willing to make things better for New Mexico"; cites passing bipartisan legislation.

S6NM01186.name: Larry Marker
S6NM01186.bio: Has worked in oil and gas production, farming, ranching, manufacturing, construction, and service.

positions.stance: Supports an all-of-the-above strategy, stopping federal permitting overreach, and making New Mexico a leader in oil, gas, hydrogen, and nuclear.
Supports shutting down the fentanyl pipeline, backing Border Patrol and local police, and opposing policies that shield violent offenders.
Opposes regulatory abuse against farmers and ranchers and defends grazing rights, water access, and working land.

S6NE00129.name: Pete Ricketts
S6NE00129.bio: U.S. Senator for Nebraska and former governor of Nebraska.

positions.stance: Says he is helping Nebraska families, workers, seniors, and small business owners "keep more of their hard-earned income."
Voted for $46.5 billion in border security and to hire 16,000 border patrol agents.
Calls Communist China a threat; introduced legislation to stop foreign adversaries from owning U.S. farmland.
Highlights cutting state spending growth as governor by rooting out waste and inefficiency.
Working "to bring our Proven Nebraska Solutions to the rest of America."

S8ID00092.name: Jim Risch
S8ID00092.bio: U.S. Senator for Idaho; former Idaho governor, lieutenant governor, and Ada County prosecuting attorney.

positions.stance: Says Idaho's public lands, from hunting and recreation to logging and grazing, "are essential to our way of life."
"To keep the American Dream within reach for Idaho families, we must tackle rising costs."
Calls small businesses "the backbone of our economy and the lifeblood of our communities."
A farmer and beef producer who pledges to fight for Idaho's agricultural families.
"A nation without secure borders is not sovereign."
Says agriculture is a priority industry and the wellbeing of the American farmer must be prioritized.
"Candidates should not be allowed to take money from foreign governments or corporations."
Says investing in the health, safety, welfare, and education of children must be the number one priority.
"End special treatment for hyperscale data centers."
Says the economy thrives where human rights are protected and labor is rewarded fairly.

S6NH00141.name: Chris Pappas
S6NH00141.bio: U.S. Representative, former New Hampshire Executive Councilor, and former manager of his family's Manchester restaurant.

positions.stance: Fighting to lower costs on utilities and groceries and make child care, health care, and housing more affordable.
Supports closing loopholes that let current and former officials get rich off their positions.
Supports increasing access to Pell grants, affordable community college, and debt forgiveness for students entering high-demand careers.
Supports an all-of-the-above energy strategy and investment in lower-cost clean energy, and calls climate change an existential threat.
"No one should be discriminated against for who they love or choose to marry."

S6NH00208.name: John E. Sununu
S6NH00208.bio: Engineer and former manufacturing company operations executive who previously represented New Hampshire in Congress.

S6ME00464.name: Troy Jackson
S6ME00464.bio: Former logger and former Maine Senate President who served twenty years in the legislature.

positions.stance: "Troy believes health care is a right, not a privilege"; supports Medicare for All.
Supports lowering prescription drug costs: "No Mainer should have to choose between filling a prescription and paying their bills."
Supports taxing billionaires and making large corporations pay their fair share.
Wants a tax code that "puts more money back in the pockets of working and middle-class families" and will fight to cut taxes for working families.
Supports dismantling and abolishing ICE.

S6MT00295.name: Kurt Alme
S6MT00295.bio: Former Montana Budget Director and Department of Revenue Director, and former prosecutor.

S6MT00253.name: Alani Bankhead
S6MT00253.bio: Retired Air Force lieutenant colonel and former federal supervisory special agent.

positions.stance: Supports banning congressional stock trading, the DISCLOSE Act, congressional term limits, and town halls in every Montana county.
"No one is above the law"; supports restoring checks and balances, War Powers limits, and enforcement of court orders.
"Montana runs Montana's elections"; supports restoring the Voting Rights Act and keeping the president out of state voter files.
"A Montana paycheck should be able to buy a Montana home"; supports taxing hedge-fund purchases of single-family homes.
Supports universal health care that runs through private doctors and community hospitals.

S6RI00163.name: Jack Reed
S6RI00163.bio: U.S. Senator for Rhode Island and former Army Ranger who commanded paratroopers in the 82nd Airborne.

S4RI00051.name: Raymond McKay
S4RI00051.bio: Former network and telecommunications manager for the City of Warwick for 26 years.

positions.stance: Supports growing the economy for the benefit of all and stemming inflation.
Supports strengthening Social Security and Medicare by stopping deficit spending and balancing the budget.
Supports repealing laws that "threaten personal and parental freedoms and free markets."
Supports securing the borders, "prioritizing the best interests of Rhode Islanders and Americans first."

S0DE00092.name: Chris Coons
S0DE00092.bio: U.S. Senator for Delaware and former county government official.

positions.stance: Says many Delawareans are struggling to afford rent or buy a home.
Supports investments in education and workforce training programs.
Believes "everyone should have access to quality, affordable health care" and has fought threats to the Affordable Care Act and Medicaid.
Cites working closely with law enforcement while in county government.
Says American foreign policy "is fundamentally about ensuring our security and protecting our prosperity."

S6DE00206.name: Michael Katz
S6DE00206.bio: Physician and pediatric critical care anesthesiologist.

positions.stance: "Halt wasteful spending, cut red tape, and lower energy and housing costs for Delaware families."
"Lower drug costs, fix rural care gaps, and shift the system from treating illness to preventing it."
"Cut federal red tape, lock in pro-growth taxes, and bring critical manufacturing home."
"Expand early childhood, align education with the modern workforce, and close the zip-code gap."
Supports "a strong military, honored veterans, a modern VA, and a nation that stands with allies and up to adversaries."
